mainTopic: Valid סכך materials, natural versus tied bundles, marsh מרור, and how many items make a binding (אגד)
overview: This amud discusses which plants may be used as סכך, and when tied plants count as a forbidden bundle. It opens with a reason from the previous page: a material that makes a person leave the סוכה, for example because it smells bad, cannot be used. אביי applies this reasoning to thorns and shrubs. He allows thorns but forbids shrubs, because their falling leaves drive people out. רב and רבינא בר שילא allow palm-tree and reed offshoots, which grow joined together. They give two reasons: a binding made by Heaven is not a binding, and a single tie on something already joined is not a binding either. A ברייתא supports the ruling on reeds once its wording is corrected. In a side discussion, רבינא בר שילא rules that marsh bitter herbs are valid for מרור on פסח. אביי and רבא each defend this against a ברייתא that disqualifies אזוב with an added name. Finally, רב חסדא defines a binding: one item is not a binding, three items are, and two items depend on a מחלוקת between רבי יוסי and the רבנן about the bundle of אזוב. The amud ends with a question about a ברייתא that seems to contradict itself; the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing reason: foul-smelling materials make a person leave
steps.stepSummary: The previous discussion ends with its reason: once the materials start to smell bad, a person will abandon the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since their smell goes bad, a person leaves the סוכה and goes out.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the discussion from the previous page. It gives the reason why certain materials cannot be used as סכך: they start to smell, and people will leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule here is not about what the material is made of. It is about whether a person can comfortably stay in the סוכה. A סוכה that a person will run away from is not a proper סוכה. This same reason will be used again in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: He abandons them (the סוכה) and goes out

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key principle for the whole section: a material that will drive a person out of the סוכה is not fit for סכך.

phrases.english: since their smell becomes foul —
phrases.notes: This finishes the reason that started on the previous page.

phrases.english: one abandons them and goes out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning of a statement that began on the previous amud
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A material whose smell goes bad cannot be used as סכך, because people will leave the סוכה.

steps.title: רב חנן בר רבא permits thorns and shrubs
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר רבא rules that both thorns (היזמי) and shrubs (היגי) may be used as סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר רבא said: these thorns and shrubs may be used to cover the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רב חנן בר רבא says that two kinds of plants, thorns and shrubs, are both fine for סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are plants that grow from the ground and are no longer attached to it. So by the basic rules of סכך, both should be valid. His ruling does not treat the practical problem of falling leaves as a reason to disqualify them.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of shrub or brushwood that drops its leaves
We may use as סכך (to roof the סוכה)

phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Rava said:
these thorns and shrubs —
one may roof the סוכה with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling about another type of material, following the theme of the previous discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thorns and shrubs are both valid for סכך.

steps.title: אביי permits thorns but not shrubs
steps.stepSummary: אביי disagrees in part. Thorns are permitted, but shrubs are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: we may use thorns as סכך, but we may not use shrubs.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different ruling. He agrees about thorns but says shrubs may not be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי splits רב חנן בר רבא's ruling into two. Thorns stay permitted, but shrubs are excluded. The גמרא will next ask why shrubs are different.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not use it as סכך

phrases.english: Abaye said:
with thorns — we roof the סוכה;
with shrubs — we do not roof the סוכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing, narrower ruling than רב חנן בר רבא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thorns are valid for סכך; shrubs are not.

steps.title: Why are shrubs not allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind אביי's ruling against shrubs.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why אביי forbids shrubs. This short question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shrubs are plants, so by the basic rules they should be valid. The question is therefore what practical problem makes them unfit.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind אביי's distinction
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why shrubs are disqualified even though they are valid plant material

steps.title: Shrubs drop their leaves, so a person will leave
steps.stepSummary: Shrubs shed their leaves into the סוכה, so a person will abandon it and go out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since their leaves fall off, a person abandons the סוכה and goes out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that shrub leaves keep falling down onto the people and food in the סוכה. Because of that, people will leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same logic as Step 1. A material that makes the סוכה unpleasant to stay in is disqualified. With foul-smelling materials the problem was smell; here it is falling leaves.
steps.whatToRemember: Shrubs (היגי) are disqualified for a practical reason, not because they are the wrong kind of material. Falling leaves will make people leave the סוכה.

phrases.english: since their leaves fall off,
one abandons it (the סוכה) and goes out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Shrubs shed their leaves, which drives a person out of the סוכה.

steps.title: רב permits the offshoot of a palm tree
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל in the name of רב rules that the offshoot of a palm tree may be used as סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: this offshoot of the palm tree may be used to cover the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins about a palm-tree offshoot, a piece from which several branches grow out together. רב says it is valid סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is that the branches are joined together at their base, so they could look like a bundle. Earlier, the משנה taught that bundles (חבילות) may not be used as סכך. The next two steps explain why this offshoot is still allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: An offshoot, a piece from which several branches come out

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
this offshoot of the palm tree —
one may roof the סוכה with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling about another material
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A palm-tree offshoot is valid for סכך.

steps.title: A natural binding is not a binding
steps.stepSummary: Even though the branches are joined, a joining made by Heaven (natural growth) does not count as a bundle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though they are bound together, a binding made by Heaven is not called a binding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken problem: the branches are tied together, so why is this not a forbidden bundle? The answer is that they grew that way naturally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on bundles applies to bundles that people tie. Branches that grow joined together are a 'binding by Heaven' and are not counted as a bundle at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A binding by Heaven, meaning natural growth

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying that bundles are allowed. A bundle tied by a person is still forbidden. Only a natural joining is not counted as a bundle.

phrases.english: Even though they are bound,
a binding by the hands of Heaven
is not called a binding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב's ruling against the anticipated objection of the bundle rule
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the category: natural joining is not a bundle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the branches are joined, the offshoot might be a forbidden bundle
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a person-made binding counts; a natural joining does not

steps.title: Adding one tie does not make a bundle
steps.stepSummary: Even if a person also ties the far ends of the branches, a single added binding does not count as a bundle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though he then ties them again, a binding into one is not called a binding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא handles a second worry: what if a person ties the loose ends of the branches together? It says this still does not make a forbidden bundle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a person did make a tie, so the first answer about natural growth is not enough. The answer is that tying together something already joined, or making only one tie, is not a real bundle. Some explain that a real bundle needs ties in two places, so one human tie does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: A binding into one, or a single binding

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דַּהֲדַר אָגֵיד לְהוּ,
phrases.english: Even though one then binds them again,
a binding into one (a single binding)
is not called a binding.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דַּהֲדַר אָגֵיד לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second protection for the case where a person also ties the branches
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the definition of a bundle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once a person ties the other end, it becomes a person-made bundle
steps.terutzMaskana: A single tie, or tying what is already joined, does not create a bundle

steps.title: רבינא בר שילא permits offshoots of reeds
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא in the name of רבינא בר שילא rules that reed offshoots may be used as סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of רבינא בר שילא: these offshoots of reeds may be used to cover the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: A parallel teaching begins about reeds that grow out together from one base. They are permitted just like the palm offshoot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reed offshoots raise the same problem as the palm offshoot, because the stalks are joined. The same two explanations will follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Offshoots, clusters growing from one base

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רָבִינָא בַּר שֵׁילָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Ravina bar Sheila said:
these offshoots of reeds —
one may roof the סוכה with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רָבִינָא בַּר שֵׁילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling to רב's ruling about the palm offshoot
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reed offshoots are valid for סכך.

steps.title: Reeds joined naturally are not a bundle
steps.stepSummary: The reeds' natural joining is a binding by Heaven, which does not count as a bundle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though they are bound, a binding made by Heaven is not called a binding.
steps.whatsHappening: The same first answer is given for the reeds. They grew joined, so they are not a forbidden bundle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the principle from Step 7 for a new case. It shows that the rule about natural binding is general and is not limited to palm trees.

phrases.english: Even though they are bound —
a binding by the hands of Heaven
is not called a binding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the Step 7 principle to reeds
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the category: natural joining is not a bundle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Joined reeds might be a forbidden bundle
steps.terutzMaskana: A natural joining is not a bundle

steps.title: An added single tie on reeds still does not make a bundle
steps.stepSummary: Even if a person ties the reeds' other end, a single binding does not count as a bundle, so the reeds stay valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though he then ties them again, a binding into one is not called a binding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the reed teaching with the same second answer. A person's added tie does not turn the reeds into a forbidden bundle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This completes the parallel with the palm offshoot. Both cases are protected by the same two principles: a natural binding is not a binding, and a single added tie is not a binding.

keyTerms.meaning: A bundle, which is forbidden as סכך (background term from the משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: Palm offshoots and reed offshoots are valid סכך for two reasons. A joining by Heaven is not a bundle, and a single tie on something already joined is not a bundle. Thorns are valid, but shrubs are not, because their leaves fall and drive people out.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דַּהֲדַר אָגֵיד לְהוּ —
phrases.english: Even though one then binds them again —
a binding into one (a single binding)
is not called a binding.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דַּהֲדַר אָגֵיד לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the Step 8 principle to reeds and closes the parallel
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Reed offshoots, like palm offshoots, are valid סכך even if a person adds a single tie.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the ruling on reed offshoots
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a ברייתא saying that קנים and דוקרנין may be used as סכך, as support for רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: Reeds and reed offshoots — one may use them for סכך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to back up רב חסדא's ruling that reed offshoots are valid סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said reed offshoots are kosher סכך even though they grow joined together. Now a ברייתא names דוקרנין (offshoots) as valid סכך, which matches his ruling. The wording of the ברייתא will be questioned in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא that supports what was just said)
Pointed offshoots that grow out of a reed stalk
One may use them as סכך (roofing for the סוכה)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
phrases.notes: This is how the גמרא brings in a ברייתא that backs up what was just said.

phrases.english: Reeds and offshoots — one may roof with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support the conclusion of step 11 that reed offshoots are valid סכך.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's ruling that reed offshoots may be used as סכך
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing קנים and דוקרנין as valid סכך

steps.title: Why would the ברייתא need to say reeds are valid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that it is obvious plain reeds are valid סכך, so listing them is unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reeds? That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the wording of the ברייתא. Plain reeds clearly qualify as סכך, so why mention them at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain reeds grow from the ground, have been cut off, and cannot become טמא. That makes them the most basic valid סכך. A ברייתא should not waste words teaching something obvious, so the wording must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (an objection that a statement teaches nothing new)

phrases.english: Reeds — that is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא cited in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word קנים in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Plain reeds are obviously valid סכך, so the ברייתא would not need to say so.

steps.title: Reread the ברייתא as 'offshoots of reeds'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the reading: the ברייתא means reeds of offshoots, meaning reed offshoots, are valid סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: Reeds of offshoots (reed offshoots) — one may use them for סכך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by adjusting the wording. The ברייתא is not talking about two separate things. It is talking about one thing: offshoots that grow from reeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After this change, the ברייתא no longer teaches the obvious point about plain reeds. It teaches the new point that joined reed offshoots are valid. That is exactly רב חסדא's ruling, so the support now fully works.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (a correction to how a text should be read)

steps.whatToRemember: Reed offshoots are valid סכך. רב חסדא says so, and a ברייתא backs him up once it is read correctly as 'reeds of offshoots.'

phrases.english: Say instead: reeds of offshoots
one may roof with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: קָנִים שֶׁל דּוּקְרָנִין מְסַכְּכִין בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 13 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists plain reeds and offshoots as two separate items, so mentioning reeds would be pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks only about reed offshoots, which directly supports רב חסדא.

steps.title: Marsh bitter herbs are valid for מרור on פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting רבינא בר שילא, rules that bitter herbs that grow in a marsh can be used for the מרור obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said in the name of רבינא בר שילא: These bitter herbs of the marsh — a person fulfills his obligation with them on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling from the same chain of teachers. This one is about מרור, not סכך: marsh bitter herbs count for the מרור of פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling appears here only because it was said by the same speakers, רב חסדא quoting רבינא בר שילא. The new point is that this herb is valid for מרור even though its name has an extra description, 'of the marsh.' That detail is what the next step will attack.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רָבִינָא בַּר שֵׁילָא:
phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said that Ravina bar Sheila said:
These bitter herbs of the marsh —

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם יוֹצֵא בָּהֶן יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח.
phrases.english: a person fulfills his obligation with them on Passover.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רָבִינָא בַּר שֵׁילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic linked only because the speakers are the same as in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marsh bitter herbs are valid for the מצוה of מרור on פסח.

steps.title: Challenge from the rule that אזוב with an added name is invalid
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules out any kind of אזוב with a descriptive name, which suggests marsh מרור should also be invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: For a מצוה that needs אזוב, one uses plain אזוב. Not Greek אזוב, not stibium אזוב, not desert אזוב, not Roman אזוב, and not any אזוב that has an added name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא with a ברייתא about אזוב. The ברייתא says that when the תורה names a plant, a variety with an extra descriptive name does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets a general rule: a plant with a qualifying name, such as 'X of a certain kind,' is not the plain plant the תורה means. Using the same logic, 'bitter herbs of the marsh' has an added name. So it should not count as the מרור the תורה requires.

keyTerms.meaning: Hyssop, a plant used in several מצוות
An added or qualifying name, such as 'Greek' or 'desert'

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is about אזוב, not מרור. The גמרא is using its general rule about added names and applying it to marsh מרור.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Hyssop,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֵזוֹב יוֹן, וְלֹא אֵזוֹב כּוֹחֳלִי,
phrases.english: and not Greek hyssop, and not stibium hyssop,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֵזוֹב מִדְבָּרִי, וְלֹא אֵזוֹב רוֹמִי,
phrases.english: and not desert hyssop, and not Roman hyssop,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֵזוֹב שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שֵׁם לְוַוי.
phrases.english: and not any hyssop that has a modifying name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 15 using a ברייתא about אזוב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא בר שילא's ruling that marsh מרור is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A plant with an added name, a שם לווי, does not count for a מצוה. 'Marsh bitter herbs' has such a name, so it should not count as מרור.

steps.title: אביי: added names only matter if they existed before מתן תורה
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that a qualifying name disqualifies a plant only if the varieties already had different names before מתן תורה. Bitter herbs never had that.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Any plant whose name was already split into varieties before מתן תורה, and then the תורה came and was particular about one of them, we know that the other varieties have a qualifying name and are invalid. But these bitter herbs never had separate names before מתן תורה at all.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by showing that אזוב and מרור are different cases. With אזוב, the names already separated the varieties. With מרור, every kind was simply called 'bitter herbs.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With אזוב, people already called the different varieties by separate names before the תורה was given. So when the תורה said 'אזוב,' it chose the plain kind and excluded the others. Bitter herbs never had separate names back then, so when the תורה said 'מרור' it included every kind, and marsh מרור stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Its name was changed or set apart from the plain name
The giving of the תורה at הר סיני
Was particular about it, meaning the תורה chose a specific kind

steps.whatToRemember: Not every descriptive word disqualifies a plant. An added name only matters if the varieties already had separate names before מתן תורה, like אזוב. מרור never did, so marsh bitter herbs are valid on פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: אביי gives a general test for reading plant names in the תורה. It applies wherever a מצוה requires a specific species.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּנָּה שְׁמוֹ קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Any plant whose name was differentiated before the giving of the Torah,
and the Torah came and was particular about it —
it is known that it has a modifying name.
But these, their names were not differentiated
before the giving of the Torah at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כֹּל שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּנָּה שְׁמוֹ קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 by showing that the אזוב rule does not apply to מרור.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any plant with a descriptive name, including marsh מרור, is excluded, just as with אזוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only names that already set varieties apart before מתן תורה disqualify a plant. Bitter herbs had no such names, so marsh מרור is valid.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבינא בר שילא's ruling stands: marsh bitter herbs are valid for מרור on פסח.

steps.title: רבא: the extra name only tells where the plant grows
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer to the question from the אזוב ברייתא. The plant's real name is just 'bitter herbs.' 'Of the marsh' is only a description of where it is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: These plants are simply called 'bitter herbs.' People call them 'bitter herbs of the marsh' only because they are found in the marsh.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the same question אביי answered, but in a different way. He says marsh bitter herbs do not really have a separate name at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the descriptive name does not matter, because the name did not exist before מתן תורה. רבא says there is no true second name in the first place. 'Of the marsh' is just a casual description of location, like saying 'apples from the orchard.' So the rule from the ברייתא, which rules out אזוב with a descriptive name, does not apply here at all.
steps.whatToRemember: Marsh bitter herbs are valid for מרור. אביי says this is because their name was not a separate name before מתן תורה. רבא says it is because 'marsh' only describes where they grow, not what kind of plant they are.

phrases.english: Rava said:
These: their name is simply 'bitter herbs,'
and the fact that people call them 'bitter herbs of the marsh'
is because they are found in the marsh.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הָנֵי מְרָרְיָתָא סְתָמָא שְׁמַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer, different from אביי's in step 17, to the קשיא in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the descriptive phrase is not a real name
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Bitter herbs of the marsh' looks like a named variety, which would be invalid like the named kinds of אזוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The name is only 'bitter herbs.' The word 'marsh' just describes location, so the plant is valid.

steps.title: רב חסדא: how many items make a binding
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that tying one item is not a binding, three items is a binding, and two items depends on a מחלוקת between רבי יוסי and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Tying a single item is not called a binding. Three items is called a binding. Two items is a dispute between רבי יוסי and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ruling from רב חסדא. He defines how many items must be tied together before they count as a 'binding.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the rule in our פרק that tied bundles may not be used as סכך. רב חסדא gives the number. One item, even tied with a knot, is never a binding. Three items always is. Two items is unclear, and he links it to an existing מחלוקת. The next step cites that source.

keyTerms.meaning: A binding, items tied together into a bundle

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether a bundle counts as a binding decides whether it can be used for סכך. The same idea of 'binding' appears in other מצוות, such as tying the לולב.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
If one bound a single item, it is not called a binding.
Three items are called a binding.
Two items are a dispute between Rabbi Yosei and the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אֶיגֶד בְּחַד לָא שְׁמֵיהּ אֶגֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the מרור digression to the binding (אגד) theme of steps 6–11. רב חסדא here defines the phrase he earlier quoted from רבינא בר שילא 'אֶיגֶד בְּחַד לָא שְׁמֵיהּ אֶגֶד' and adds the cases of three and two items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One item is not a binding. Three items is a binding. Two items depends on the מחלוקת between רבי יוסי and the רבנן.

steps.title: The source: the משנה about the bundle of hyssop
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the bundle of אזוב. This is the source for the dispute about two items.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: The מצוה of אזוב needs three stalks, with three stems on them. רבי יוסי says: The מצוה of אזוב is three stems. If some broke off, the remaining two are still fine. Even the leftover stumps of any size are fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה that רב חסדא was pointing to. It shows where רבי יוסי and the רבנן disagree about how many pieces the אזוב bundle needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אזוב was tied into a bundle for sprinkling, for example for purifying from טומאת מת. The תנא קמא, the רבנן, says the bundle needs three stalks. רבי יוסי also mentions three, but says that if pieces break off, two remaining stems are still fine, and even small stumps are fine. The משנה does not say clearly whether 'three' is required or only ideal. The next step works that out.

keyTerms.meaning: Hyssop, a plant tied in a bundle and used for sprinkling in purification rituals
Stems, or the top shoots on each stalk
Its remnants, what is left after some pieces broke off

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different ideas here. 'Its beginning' (תחילתו) is how many pieces you need when you first tie the bundle. 'Its remnants' (שיריו) is what is enough if some later broke off. Keep them separate.

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah:
The מצוה of hyssop is three stalks
and on them three stems.
Rabbi Yosei says:
The מצוה of hyssop is three stems,
and its remnants may be two,
and its stumps may be any size.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source of the מחלוקת that רב חסדא mentioned.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that a binding of two items is a dispute between רבי יוסי and the רבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the מצוה of אזוב (משנה פרה)

steps.title: First guess: רבי יוסי says three is only ideal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא's first reading is this. Since רבי יוסי accepts two leftover stems, he must accept two at the start, and three is only the ideal. So the רבנן, who argue with him, must require three.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first we thought: since רבי יוסי says the leftovers can be two, the bundle can also start with two. When he says 'three,' he means that is the best way to do the מצוה. And since רבי יוסי says three is only ideal, the רבנן must hold that three is required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a first guess about which side holds what in the משנה. Notice the opening words 'קא סלקא דעתין,' 'we thought.' This tells you a challenge is coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic: if two remnants are enough, then two must be enough from the start, so רבי יוסי's 'three' is only לכתחילה. The רבנן disagree with him, so they must hold that three is needed even after the fact (לעכב). Under this reading, רבי יוסי treats two items as a binding and the רבנן do not.

keyTerms.meaning: It entered our minds, a first assumption that will soon be tested
Its beginning, how many pieces it had when first tied
For the ideal way of doing the מצוה; not strictly required
Required; without it the מצוה is invalid

phrases.english: It entered our minds:
since its remnants may be two,
its beginning may also be two,
and the fact that it teaches 'three' is for the ideal מצוה.
And since for Rabbi Yosei three is only ideal,
for the Rabbis three is required.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתִּין מִדִּשְׁיָרָיו שְׁנַיִם תְּחִילָּתוֹ נָמֵי שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the משנה from step 20 to explain how the two sides divide.
steps.raayaObject: Which side holds that two items count as a binding
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from רבי יוסי's ruling that two remnants are enough

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יוסי requires three
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי saying a bundle that started with two is invalid. It is valid only if it started with three. This contradicts the guess that he holds three is only ideal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches that רבי יוסי says: If the אזוב started with two and one is left, it is invalid. It is valid only if it started with three and two are left!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the guess from the last step. It brings a ברייתא where רבי יוסי clearly requires three pieces at the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guess said that for רבי יוסי two is fine from the start. This ברייתא says the opposite: starting with two is invalid. Two remnants are enough only because the bundle began with three. So the step 21 reasoning that 'two remnants means two is enough at the start' falls apart.

phrases.english: But it was taught in a Baraita: Rabbi Yosei says:
Hyssop whose beginning was two
and whose remnants are one is invalid,
and it is valid only when
its beginning was three and its remnants are two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading proposed in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that for רבי יוסי three is only ideal and two is enough at the start
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit ברייתא has רבי יוסי rule that a bundle starting with two is invalid, so for him three is required.

steps.title: Reverse the opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא switches the positions. For רבי יוסי three is required. For the רבנן three is only ideal, so two still works after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it: according to רבי יוסי three is required, and according to the רבנן three is only the ideal way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by flipping who holds what. This now fits the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ברייתא shows רבי יוסי requires three, the רבנן who argue with him must hold that three is only ideal. That means two works for them after the fact. So for רב חסדא's question, two items count as a binding according to the רבנן, but not according to רבי יוסי.
steps.whatToRemember: One tied item is never a binding. Three always is. Two is a binding according to the רבנן, for whom three is only ideal. It is not a binding according to רבי יוסי, for whom three is required.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not keep the first guess from step 21. After 'איפוך,' it is רבי יוסי who requires three, and the רבנן who accept two after the fact.

phrases.english: Reverse it:
according to Rabbi Yosei, three is required;
according to the Rabbis, three is only ideal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 22 by switching the opinions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי holds three is only ideal, and the רבנן require three.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי requires three. The רבנן hold three is only ideal, so two counts as a binding for them after the fact.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the switched view of the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a bundle of אזוב that started with two stems and was left with one is כשר. It is פסול only if it was one stem from start to finish. This fits the רבנן as the גמרא now understands them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: A bundle of אזוב that started with two stems and was left with one is כשר. It is only פסול when it was just one stem at the start and one stem at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the new reading from the last step: for the רבנן, two stems at the start are enough after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23 the גמרא said that for the רבנן three stems are only the ideal. This ברייתא accepts a bundle that started with just two, so it must follow the רבנן and not רבי יוסי, who requires three. It also says a bundle is פסול only when it was a single stem the whole time.

keyTerms.meaning: Hyssop, the plant tied in a bundle for sprinkling
Its beginning, how many stems it had at the start
Its leftovers, the stems still left later

steps.confusionAlert: The word וְהָתַנְיָא often opens a challenge. Here it opens a support. The ברייתא backs up the switched view of the רבנן from step 23.

phrases.english: And so it was taught in a baraita:
Hyssop whose beginning was two stems
and its leftovers are one stem is fit,
and it is not unfit unless
its beginning and its leftovers are one stem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the switched positions from step 23 by showing a ברייתא that fits the רבנן's view.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that for the רבנן three stems are only the ideal, so a bundle that started with two works after the fact.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: an אזוב bundle that started with two and was left with one is כשר. It is פסול only if it was one from start to end.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself about one leftover stem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the end of the ברייתא makes one leftover stem פסול, but the beginning made one leftover stem כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a bundle with one leftover stem פסול? But you just said a bundle with one leftover stem is כשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds what looks like a contradiction inside the ברייתא itself. The answer comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part says a bundle left with one stem is כשר. The last part mentions a bundle left with one stem and calls it פסול. The גמרא asks how the same ברייתא can give both rulings about one leftover stem.

keyTerms.meaning: But you said, which points back to an earlier statement

phrases.english: Its leftovers are one, and it is unfit?
But you said that if its leftovers are one, it is fit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the ברייתא just brought as support and asks about its wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the ברייתא from step 24.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first part rules that one leftover stem is כשר. The last part rules that one leftover stem is פסול. Both cannot be true unless the two cases are told apart.
